interpretation.recommendation: Every candidate remains insufficient-evidence for recommendation. The comparison standardizes missingness; it does not convert research depth, organizational scale, ratings, contracts, or service outputs into an impact score.
interpretation.translationBoundary: “Life substantially bettered” remains undefined for San Francisco until a versioned model publishes the threshold, duration, moral weights, counterfactual, uncertainty range, model date, and sensitivity analysis.
interpretation.fundingBoundary: A donation page or organization-wide budget is not room for more funding. Each gift-size scenario remains unavailable until a reviewed, time-bounded marginal plan identifies what additional funding would buy and what other funding it may displace.

candidates.name: GLIDE
candidates.interventionType: meals, housing navigation, behavioral health, family programs, outreach, and advocacy
candidates.serviceGeography: Tenderloin, San Francisco, and the broader Bay Area; city contracts confirm multiple local programs.
candidates.decisionSummary: GLIDE has exceptional reach across food, housing, benefits, and behavioral health, and several underlying intervention families have credible external evidence. Its FY2025 public reporting still combines service volume, administrative connections, multiple funding streams, and several distinct programs. No accepted source identifies which intervention a new private gift would expand or the durable, additional outcome it would buy.

candidates.name: GrowSF
candidates.interventionType: voter information, candidate support, policy research, and electoral advocacy
candidates.decisionSummary: GrowSF reports substantial June 2026 voter-guide and paid-media reach, three aligned candidate victories, and an aligned ballot-measure result. Neither record identifies votes changed by GrowSF, the election counterfactual, policy implementation, or downstream effects on San Franciscans, so cost-effectiveness and room for more funding remain unestimated.

candidates.name: Housing Action Coalition
candidates.interventionType: housing policy research, project endorsements, coalition building, litigation strategy, and legislative advocacy
candidates.serviceGeography: California with Bay Area and San Francisco advocacy; reported impacts are not SF-only.
candidates.decisionSummary: HAC reports a substantial 2024 advocacy portfolio, including three sponsored bills signed into law and Housing Element work that made more than 4,500 homes legally feasible. Public records confirm at least one flagship bill reached chaptered status, and external housing research supports a plausible path from actual construction to lower nearby rents and displacement pressure. The accepted evidence does not estimate HAC's contribution to those policy outcomes, the share of legal capacity that will become occupied homes, or what a new restricted gift would change.
